rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, an owner may not end a tenancy without just cause, and the cause must be stated in a written notice. Just cause includes at-fault causes (such as nonpayment of rent, breach of a material lease term, nuisance, criminal activity) and no-fault causes (such as owner move-in, withdrawal of the property from the rental market, demolition or substantial remodel). Before a just-cause termination notice, the owner must first give notice of the violation and time to fix it. For no-fault terminations, the owner must provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive rent for the final 3 months. Owners must notify tenants of the protections.
